NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491 and
  proposed Resolution No. 2493, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social
  distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely
  via teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may
  participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 849 7088 0788 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 849 7088 0788, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES

  JANUARY 25, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:08 pm remotely via teleconference, in accordance with
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491 and
proposed Resolution 2493, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead

  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF OUTGOING COMMISSION & COMMITTEE MEMBERS

The following retiring Commissioners and Committee Members were recognized for their
years of service:

  •  Tim Scott, Planning Commissioner for 14 years
  •  Tim Zigrang, Planning Commissioner for 6 years (in attendance)
  •  Debora Chan-Southwell, Environmental Advisory Committee Member for 13 years
  •  Arthur Wisot, Environmental Advisory Committee Member for one year, Traffic &
  Safety Committee Member for 25 years (in attendance)

B.  EMPLOYEE SERVICE AWARDS

Administrative Assistant Carol Corea was recognized for 5 years of employment with the
City of Rolling Hills Estates.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

 7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2494 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF FY 2022 23
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any
  public testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; 4) waive further reading and approve
  Resolution No. 2494 authorizing execution of a contract with the Los Angeles County
  Community Development Commission for participation in the program for funding of
  the ADA Access Ramp and Sidewalk Improvement Program as identified in the
  Program and Conditions Assessment Report dated April 2, 2014 in the amount of
  approximately $29,889.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, to open the public hearing.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that there is an additional $105,000 in General Fund
money budgeted for this project and other sidewalk repairs that are needed throughout the
year, which are reported to the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN confirmed this would include both ADA access ramps and
sidewalk improvements.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  to close the public hearing.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2494 AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF A
  CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM
  FOR FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS RAMP AND SIDEWALK
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE PROGRAM AND
  CONDITIONS ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL 2, 2014 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF APPROXIMATELY $29,889.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210363: DRAFT GENERAL PLAN 2040 AND FINAL
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (FEIR) LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) take public
  testimony; 3.) discuss the issues related to the Draft General Plan 2040 and Final
  Program Environmental Impact Report; 4) close the Public Hearing; and 5) adopt
  Resolution No. 2496, certifying the Rolling Hills Estates 2040 General Plan Final
  Environmental Impact Report (SCH # 202105450, adopting the Findings of Fact and
  a Statement of Overriding Considerations, and a Mitigation Monitoring and Report
  Program; and 6) adopt Resolution No. 2497, adopting the Rolling Hills Estates 2040
  General Plan and 2021-2029 Housing Element.

Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), and
introduced consultants from Michael Baker International, Fehr & Peers, Sapphos
Environmental, Inc., Alta Planning + Design and Veronica Tam & Associates.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 25, 2022
 Consultant John Bellas of Michael Baker International presented a summary of the General
Plan process that has taken place over the last five years.

Consultant Surabhi Barbhaya of Michael Baker International presented a summary of the
General Plan Update’s eight elements, Vision Statement and Guiding Principals, the General
Plan Update’s framework, reasons for proposed changes in the various areas of the City, and
notable changes to the General Plan.

Consultant Dan Wery of Michael Baker International presented a summary of the proposed
Mixed Use Overlay District and elements of the Commercial District Vision Plan.

Consultant Seth Contreras of Fehr & Peers presented a summary of the Mobility Element.

Consultant John Muggridge of Fehr & Peers presented a summary of the Sustainability
Element.

Consultant Ryan Johnson of Alta Planning + Design presented a summary of the mobility pillar
within the Sustainability Element.

Consultant Bellas concluded the presentation by presenting a summary of the Environmental
Impact Report (EIR) process, topics studied in the EIR, and additional analysis added to the
EIR related to wildfire emergency evacuation.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, to open the public hearing.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked all of the consultants for the presentation and their
work on the General Plan Update and COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ for her leadership on
the General Plan Advisory Committee.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern about the wildfire evacuation portion of
the presentation, and the challenges the City faces to evacuate residents quickly in the event
of a wildfire or other disaster.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF echoed COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA’s concerns and stated
she would like to see more focus on this topic.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that the General Plan and EIR on a whole are
very good, but there is room for improvement.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked the consultants and staff for their hard work during
this process, and the community for their involvement in this process.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN expressed his concern about the evacuation of the City during a major
disaster. He also noted that many portions of the Sustainability Element have already been
implemented by the City. He expressed concerns about the businesses on Bart Earle Way
if the proposed changes were to occur and confirmed with Mr. Contreras that the numbers
presented in the Mobility Element were pre-pandemic figures. He stated that he feels the
documents need further review and discussion before they are adopted.

Consultant Bellas explained that the wildfire portion was a high-level presentation in
response to previous questions and concerns, but that the consultant team could analyze
this topic in more detail should the Council desire.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN discussed concerns about ingress and egress for many
neighborhoods along Palos Verdes Drive North, and suggested a workshop be scheduled
for the Council to go through the General Plan in more detail.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ explained that this document has been reviewed in pieces
by the General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC), but that this is the first time the City
Council as a whole is reviewing the document. She agreed with the suggestion of a publicly-
noticed City Council workshop.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 25, 2022
 Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN, to close the public hearing.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO SCHEDULE A CITY COUNCIL WORKSHOP AT A
  FUTURE DATE AND TIME TO FURTHER REVIEW THE 2040 GENERAL
  PLAN FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT AND THE 2040
  GENERAL PLAN AND 2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT.

  ABSENT:  None

A.  APPEAL OF A SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT GRANTED TO ROLLING HILLS
  COVENANT CHURCH (RHCC); LOCATION: 2222 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH;
  APPLICANT: ROBERT CUBILLOS C/O OF RHCC

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct an appeal hearing for the Special
  Event Permit that was granted by staff on December 16, 2021 to the Rolling Hills
  Covenant Church (RHCC) for their outdoor parking lot tent, and uphold the Community
  Development Director’s approval of the Permit as conditioned. At the conclusion of the
  appeal hearing, unless the Council has any additional conditions that it would like added
  to the Permit, staff recommends that the issuance of the new Special Event Permit be
  affirmed with the addition of Condition No. 6 noted in the staff report.

City Attorney Davis provided a conflict of interest statement prior to beginning the appeal,
confirming that no Council Members have a conflict of interest with either the applicant or
appellant.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a brief staff report (as per
the agenda material).

Director Wahba explained the exact location of the tent, noting that it is in the back parking lot
of the church which slopes down and away from Palos Verdes Drive North, but he was not
sure of the elevation in comparison to the appellant’s residence, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER SCHMITZ. He also stated that there have been supply chain issues that have
delayed the sound blanket wall delivery, but that it was expected to be delivered by the end of
the month.

Director Wahba stated that a permit for a parking lot event with a tent such as this would have
been granted pre-pandemic, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed that the May 1 end-date of the permit is tied to the
current state of COVID. Director Wahba explained that of the other 10 parking lot event
permits issued, the Red Onion’s tent is likely the only other tent still in place, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired why sound readings were taken from the street
rather than the appellant’s yard.

Appellant Bridget Carman was given an opportunity to speak during the hearing, and
summarized the basis of her appeal, requesting the permit not be extended and that amplified
music cease.

Craig Knickerbocker was given an opportunity to speak during the hearing. He spoke on behalf
of Rolling Hills Covenant Church, explaining how services are currently being held, and

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 25, 2022
 assured the Council that as soon as it was safe to do so, they would eagerly move services
back into the Church. He also stated that the Church expects to receive the sound blanket wall
in the next ten days.

A public comment letter received by resident Rae Grieco in support of Bridget Carman’s
position was read aloud, as requested by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF discussed previous noise complaints received by the City from other
events over the last several years and the solutions and changes that were suggested and
implemented. She also discussed the church services occurring outside with amplification as
well as limited indoor services over the past 16 months, and stated that she would like to see
more communication and effort from the Church. She also made several suggestions for
reducing the noise level in the neighborhood, including moving the amplified band inside the
church, and suggested staff work with both sides to try and find a compromise.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that if the Church
requested to use amplified music at the time of their original request, that the City would have
permitted it, while reserving the right to mitigate noise if complaints were received, in response
to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN. Director Wahba also noted that amplified music is
typically only permitted for short term events.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN discussed legally allowable sound levels versus a
reasonable expectation of quiet within someone’s home. He feels the music can remain if the
sound blanket is installed, sound levels continue to meet the City’s standards and are
significantly reduced after the blanket is installed. He also stated that services should be moved
back into the church as soon as it is deemed safe, even if it is before the 5 month permit
extension date. He further discussed options to measure sound at both the Church and Ms.
Carman’s house, and small sound level adjustments that can be made to help reduce the
sound levels in the neighborhood.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN recognized the distress that Ms. Carman has been experiencing from
the noise impacts, and also recognized the important role the Rolling Hills Covenant Church
plays in the community. He stated that he values both parties as members of the community,
and would like to see a compromise found.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the latest guidance from the Los Angeles County
Health Officer Order recommends holding religious services outdoors wherever possible but
does not preclude indoor services. She stated that the Church has attempted to dampen the
sound but thinks more can be done given what Ms. Carman has been going through. She
stated that directing the two parties to work this out with the help of staff may be the best option.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted that mitigation measures have been taken in other code
enforcement matters to increase the quality of life for the individuals being impacted. She asked
the Council to recognize the impact that regular sound interruptions every single Sunday and
Tuesday, for example, would have over the course of 16 months.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed concern that amplified music was not allowed within
the original permit, however it occurred regularly with the Church services. She noted the
importance of ensuring and protecting the quiet environment that comes with living in Rolling
Hills Estates, and suggested ceasing all amplified sound for the next ten days until the sound
blanket wall can be installed by the Church.

Discussion ensued about ways to meet a reasonable compromise between both parties, and
how to proceed during the next ten days while the Church waits for the sound blanket wall to
be delivered.

City Attorney Davis explained that the permit is pending the City Council’s review and a formal
action is required by the Council; other measures can be imposed as conditions to the permit
if the Council desires.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JANUARY 25, 2022
   MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,
  AS FOLLOWS:

  REVOKE THE PERMIT WITH AMPLIFICATION UNTIL THE SOUND
  BLANKET WALL IS INSTALLED AND SOUND LEVELS ARE REANALYZED;
  SERVICES IN THE TENT AND NON-AMPLIFIED SOUND CAN CONTINUE,
  WITH THE PERMIT EXTENSION LASTING AS LONG AS NEEDED, UP TO
  FIVE MONTHS.

City Attorney Davis highlighted an issue that staff may face when “reanalyzing” the sound
levels after the sound blanket wall is installed, since sound levels are currently within the
permitted range and will remain within the permitted range, but may not necessarily be within
a range that is acceptable to the appellant.

Discussion ensued regarding potential further mitigations that could be made by the Church
to reduce sound levels, and what is plausible and acceptable to the Church in continuing
their services.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN explained that the current sound levels of the Church are legally
compliant and will be more so after the sound blanket wall is installed. He encouraged the
two parties to work together to find a compromise.

City Attorney Davis explained that the permit has been issued, therefore if the Council does
not take action, the permit stands as is, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.
